text:
alina: FYI, after the control-plane hiccup at 05:12 we started seeing a burst of NVMe write timeouts on ephemeral hosts in us-central. GPU attaches failing with device prepare timeouts. anyone on it?

mike: saw it too. agent returns 502/attach-timeout and node iowait spikes. reproduced on two hostsets.

jeff: paste the agent error you saw?

alina: agent excerpt: 
``n2026-03-21T05:13:52Z ERROR attach: timed out waiting for device prepare
root cause: nvme write timed out
``n
mike: kernel spams: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout` then `nvme: aborting command` in a loop.

janine: storage-bot flagged a scrub ramp at 05:11 for pool-ephemeral-14. concurrency jumped to 6 and throughput doubled for a minute. could be janitor overlap. :thinking_face: 

storage-bot: scrub-runner: pool-ephemeral-14 started scrub at 05:11 hostset=us-central concurrent=6 avg_throughput=380MB/s io_ps~2200

ops-sre: any SMART or temp anomalies on the affected devices?

mike: SMART ok, temps normal. controller error counters increasing: media_errors +12, crc_errors +3. Not full device-fail but correlates with timeouts.

alina: hypothesis: control-plane scheduling delay allowed janitor scrubs to collide with attach hotpath, driving io queue depth high and causing controller-level timeouts during device prepare.

jeff: mitigation: steer new GPU attaches away from the hottest machines. can we cordon/taint them?

ops-sre: cordoning top-affected hosts now. not changing kernel params clusterwide.

janine: running quick query for affected hosts: `kubectl -n infra get pods -o wide | grep ephemeral | awk '{print $7}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr`  will paste list.

mike: considering `nvme_core.nvme_max_io_queues=1` locally to reduce concurrency to controllers, but that could reduce throughput. prefer avoiding kernel fiddles unless needed.

ops-sre: draining three worst hosts and moving workloads to fallback pools.

alina: can we throttle janitor in region? drop concurrency 6->2 and pause new scrub starts for 10 minutes to let queues drain.

storage-bot: scrub-runner: concurrency reduced to 2 on pool-ephemeral-14. new scrub jobs paused for 10m.

jeff: next: run `nvme list` and `nvme error-log` on gnode-uc-14a. who can ssh?

mike: sshed into gnode-uc-14a, grabbing error-log and dmesg, uploading to triage bucket.

alina: also adding scheduling policy to block Dedicated->ephemeral attaches in us-central for 1h. revert after metrics look stable.

ops-sre: policy `routing.block.ephemeral.us-central` added for 1h. allocs will use fallback pools.

janine: pasted counts: gnode-uc-14a(8), gnode-uc-14b(6), gnode-uc-14c(5). cordoned and draining.

mike: uploaded `nvme error-log` snippet: 
``nErr cnt: 12
Status: Media Error
Cmd: 0x02 (Write)
LBA: 0x1f4a7c
```n
alina: suggests controller is overloaded, not outright failing. action items: (1) add runtime back-pressure between scrub janitor and attach flow, (2) short-circuit attaches to fallback pools when local IO saturation detected, (3) surface nvme io_ps and queue-depth metrics to routing/placement service.

jeff: also propose autoscaler rule to avoid scaling onto hosts with scrub backlog > threshold.

ops-sre: monitoring error-rate post-drain. if errors fall to baseline within 20m mark mitigated, otherwise escalate to hardware-team for detailed NVMe diagnostics.

hardware-team: on standby if escalation needed. can run full vendor diagnostics and check firmware telemetry.

alina: status update in 15m. thanks all. :thumbsup:
